_about: Published artifacts are immutable, so a defective build can never be removed — only superseded by a higher build number and/or neutralised by a metadata patch in patches/. Both of those protect FUTURE solves only: an existing pixi.lock keeps installing whatever it pinned, silently. This list is the static, self-serve record of every build known to be defective, so anyone holding a lockfile can check it (tools/check_lock.py). Keyed by exact filename; 'fixed_by' names the superseding build to re-lock onto.

libtorch-2.13.0-cuda129_repack_hf3fb3d0b.reason: depends on the shadowable name nvidia-cudnn instead of libcudnn; can silently co-install two cudnn versions at identical paths when another package constrains libcudnn (the solver then prefers this build precisely because it never mentions libcudnn) — torch dies at first conv with a version mismatch

libtorch-2.4.1-cuda124_repack_h41ae334b_.reason: carries the wheel's inherited nvidia/* RPATH entries ahead of $PREFIX/lib: a pip-installed nvidia-* wheel in the same env silently unseats every solver-chosen CUDA library

triton-3.8.0-repack_py314_h6e19f7b8_0.co.reason: vendored ptxas/cuobjdump/nvdisasm executables have no RPATH, and libMLIRDialectPlugin.so carries absolute build-machine paths plus an empty RPATH component (load-from-CWD hazard)

nvidia-cudnn-9.19.0.56-cuda12_repack_hd8.reason: deprecated name (superseded by libcudnn); ships NVIDIA binaries with zero license text despite repodata advertising LicenseRef-NVIDIA-SLA; no successor build under this name

nvidia-nvshmem-3.3.24-cuda12_repack_h95a.reason: ships NVIDIA binaries with zero license text; orphaned — no published libtorch depends on it (every cuda12 range prefers the licensed 3.4.5 build), so it is effectively unreachable, but it remains resolvable by an exact pin

libtorch-2.8.0-cuda129_repack_h327d83bf_.reason: cuda-cupti dependency window is the flavour-wide <13.0a0 instead of the exact versions proven to ship the DLL basename torch_cuda.dll imports (cupti64_2025.2.1.dll). Solves correctly today only because conda-forge ships a single build in that line; the first additional cuda-cupti build with a different basename would win the solve and break `import torch` with no solver-visible warning
